spec_deviations: Train hyperparameters are recorded as the frozen sibling-module defaults (n_iters=8, lr=3e-4, ...; L1SupervisedTrainConfig / FactSurrogateTrainConfig), and the tree omits arm-level fields (coordinate/enforcement/estimator/kernel/mechanism_backend) plus channel_scales and None-defaulted fact targets. REASON: the task binds configs to the surfaces the sibling builds actually expose, and those dataclasses own the values; the D0 trainer runtime pins production iteration counts at run time. The validator asserts equality against the dataclass defaults so the tree cannot drift (config.yaml records this as train_binding: frozen_module_defaults).

Bootstrap family_id enumeration (signflip_mandatory, axis_contrast, truncation) is recorded here as the (block, family) derivation grid with all 15 derived seeds. REASON: Annex B(a) says bootstrap seeds are 'recorded in the analyzer manifest'; E-5 records the derivation rule and values for gate-G2 disjointness and marks the analyzer manifest as the authoritative consumer. The string concatenation salt||block_id||family_id (no separator) follows the pinned formula verbatim.

Rank-seed posture is pinned to world_size=1 (rank_seed == seed). REASON: train_distributed.py derives rank_seed = seed + rank*10000, so at world_size>=3 the L1 rank-2 seeds 31000-31029 would numerically equal the K-preflight masters inside the reserved 31000-31099 block (contracts section 6 flag 5 requires this check). Single-worker posture is the conservative resolution; the overlap fact and the auxiliary rank streams (61000-61029/62000-62029) are recorded in the manifest.

negative_jump_iid exclusion is enforced by ABSENCE of a selectable dgp option (root records it under named_not_run), not by a selectable-but-flagged option. REASON: conservative, prevents accidental selection; cross-checked against E-2 D2_NAMED_NOT_RUN and the d2_series ValueError by the validator/tests.

channel_scales (s_ch) is never materialized in the tree (only a provenance string). REASON: C5/Annex B(e) pin s_ch to the hash-sealed DGP-only sample branch committed at D0; putting values in YAML would create a second unfrozen source.

Hydra packaging: composed configs nest group contents under block (with lineage/dgp nested inside), arm, axis keys (Hydra 1.3 default group packaging; absolute /group paths in block defaults). REASON: keeps groups self-describing and makes illegal combos (L1 x multiscale_logvol) unrepresentable; the validator binds to this structure explicitly.

Audit A10 is a plain YAML document (configs/reexploration/audit/a10.yaml) rather than a selectable Hydra group. REASON: it is a single audit cell that reuses B1's fixture streams (same data/init/train_kernel substreams, only the estimator differs), not a grid dimension; a group option would wrongly suggest it composes with every arm.
interface_notes: Compose a run config: hydra initialize_config_dir(config_dir='configs/reexploration', version_base='1.2') + compose(config_name='config', overrides=['block=<b1|b2|b3|b4_variant_a|b4_variant_b>', 'arm=<absolute_raw|absolute_through_m|increment_raw|increment_through_m>', 'axis=<id|pop_2x|tick_2x|kswap>']), or call ecomd.reexploration.campaign.load_composed_config(block_id, arm_id, axis_id).

Composed payload structure: payload['block'] carries block fields plus nested 'lineage' and 'dgp' groups; payload['arm'] and payload['axis'] carry their group fields; root keys (schema_version, campaign_id, mechanism_backend, estimators, eval, named_not_run, ...) carry eval-time parameters. Horizons {1,4,16,31}, K=16 draws and the 2 inference enforcements live under eval and are deployment-time, not training-time.

ecomd.reexploration.campaign public API: BLOCKS/ARMS/AXIS_SPECS/AUDIT_A10 (+ *_BY_ID dicts), enumerate_trainings() -> 450 TrainingRun, campaign_counts()/validate_counts() (raises CampaignArithmeticError), disjointness_checks()/assert_disjointness() (raises SeedCollisionError), bootstrap_seed(block_id, family_id), training_compositions()/deployment_compositions() (20/80), composed_fingerprint(payload), validate_config_tree() -> failure tuple, build_seed_manifest()/write_seed_manifest()/MANIFEST_PATH/manifest_sha256_on_disk().

Seeds: every stochastic consumer must draw from a named substream of its seed root (derive_substream_seeds / trainer substream_generator / E-2 named_substream_seed) - the 20 names and their spawn-order derivation are frozen in the manifest; no global-RNG consumers are introduced by this item.
